chunks.text: How much farmyard manure (FYM) or organic manure to apply in rice: apply about 10-12 cartloads of well-decomposed farmyard manure (FYM) or compost per hectare - roughly 4-5 cartloads per acre - along with the chemical fertilizers, or grow a green-manure crop (1 hectare is about 2.47 acres).

Recommended NPK fertilizer dose for transplanted rice on medium-fertility soil: about 80 kg nitrogen (N), 40 kg phosphorus (P2O5) and 40 kg potash (K2O) per hectare - roughly 32 kg N, 16 kg P2O5 and 16 kg K2O per acre. Apply all phosphorus and potash plus 25% of the nitrogen as basal at transplanting, then the remaining nitrogen in splits (about 50% at tillering and 25% at panicle initiation), using Urea, DAP/SSP and MOP.

How much nitrogen (urea) for rice: a rice crop needs about 80 kg N per hectare (about 32 kg N per acre) on medium-fertility soil. Rule of thumb: about 20 kg N per hectare for every 1 tonne of target yield, so a 5 t/ha crop needs about 90-100 kg N/ha. Apply 25% as basal, about 50% at tillering and about 25% at panicle initiation.

How much potash (MOP, Muriate of Potash) at panicle stage: apply about 12-16 kg of MOP per acre - roughly 20-25 kg per hectare - at panicle initiation, usually together with urea, to support grain filling and disease resistance.

How much zinc sulphate for rice: apply zinc sulphate at about 25 kg per hectare - roughly 5-10 kg per acre - as a basal dose or within 10-15 days after transplanting, on zinc-deficient soils (bronzing of leaves, stunted plants).

How much boron / Borax for rice: if boron deficiency is seen, apply Borax at about 1-2 kg per hectare (about 0.5-0.8 kg per acre) to the soil; or spray Borax as a 0.3% foliar solution (about 1-1.5 g per litre of water) before flowering, for pollen formation and grain filling.

How much phosphorus (SSP) for rice: a rice crop needs about 40 kg P per hectare (about 16 kg per acre). Single Super Phosphate (SSP) is applied as basal at land preparation, about 40-60 kg P2O5 per hectare depending on soil phosphorus.
Seed rate of Dhaincha (Sesbania aculeata) green manure: 20 kg per acre (50 kg per hectare). Sow 30-45 days before transplanting paddy and plough it in at flowering to add nitrogen and organic matter.

How much Azolla for rice: apply about 4 quintals of Azolla per acre (about 2 tonnes per hectare) in 4-6 inches of standing water 2-3 weeks before transplanting; it fixes roughly 25-30 kg N per hectare and can raise yield by 25-30%.

Fertilizer dose for a rice nursery bed: apply about 2 quintals of well-rotted FYM, 10 kg DAP, 2 kg MOP and 8 kg zinc sulphate (ZnSO4) per nursery; seedlings are ready to transplant in about 20-25 days.
